thread:
cheng: heads-up — I ran an autotune sweep overnight for kernel selection across GQA/MQA using three KV-cache layouts (interleaved, stripe, compact). sharing raw notes + a small proposal for hysteresis on fallback.

mike: nice. which hardware pools? H100 or A100?

cheng: both. H100 (v5) and A100. workload = mix of seqlen=64/256/1024; traffic split 60/30/10. batching TTL=12ms, target P95=120ms.

sara: curious about paged-attn variants you tried.

cheng: tested these kernels:
- paged-default (single-block streaming)
- paged-kvstripe (stripe layout + prefetch by stripe)
- paged-compact (tight packing, fewer pages)
- fallback: dense-kernel (no paged)

bench-bot: benchmark summary (H100, mixed MQA/GQA):
```
variant          | seqlen 64 | seqlen 256 | seqlen 1024 | kv_hit%
paged-default    | 1.2ms/tok | 2.6ms/tok   | 6.4ms/tok    | 72%
paged-kvstripe  | 1.0ms/tok | 2.3ms/tok   | 5.9ms/tok    | 83%
paged-compact   | 1.1ms/tok | 2.4ms/tok   | 6.1ms/tok    | 68%
dense-kernel    | 1.4ms/tok | 2.9ms/tok   | 8.0ms/tok    | 100%
```

cheng: kvstripe wins on throughput and hit rate for workloads with moderate locality. compact reduces memory overhead but loses some prefetch parallelism.

alyssa: what triggered fallback to dense-kernel in the sweep?

cheng: two things:
1) seqlen shift: when >40% of requests hit seqlen >=1024, paged variants start to regress on tail due to page churn.
2) KV fragmentation: interleaved layout with small blocksz (64) had higher page faults under bursty prefix patterns.

yousef: did you try block sizes beyond 64/128/256?

cheng: yes — tested 48,64,96,128,192,256. practical sweet spot was 96->128 for kvstripe on H100. 48/64 favored compact but had higher prefetch misses under MQA.

mike: any arch-specific picks? e.g., H100 prefers different kernel than A100?

cheng: small differences. H100 gains more from wider prefetch parallelism -> favors kvstripe+128. A100 is slightly better with paged-default + 96 because its memory BW and kernel-launch latency balance differs.

sara: this causes flapping if traffic oscillates — do you have a mitigation?

cheng: proposal: hysteresis + lightweight stability metric on model routes.
- maintain moving-window seqlen distribution (1k req window)
- only trigger kernel switch if new policy improves expected p95 by >6% and is stable for 2 windows
- when switching to dense fallback, set a cool-down of 10 minutes to avoid flip-flop
- allow manual override per-customer (dedicated)

alyssa: sounds reasonable. how about batching heuristics interacting with paged prefetch? any gotchas?

cheng: yes — continuous batching increases effective concurrency which helps prefetch overlap. but it also increases the number of concurrent page requests and can amplify eviction storms. heuristics:
- cap batch concurrency for paged kernels to avoid >N in-flight page refills (N=8 tuned)
- reduce join-wait TTL when page miss rate > 12% to prevent head-of-line stalls

bench-bot: additional probe numbers (A100, seqlen mix shifted to 45% >=1024):
```
variant          | p95 latency | fail_rate | kv_miss%
paged-kvstripe  | 210ms       | 0.02%     | 18%
paged-default   | 260ms       | 0.05%     | 24%
dense-kernel    | 190ms       | 0.01%     | 0%
```

cheng: takeaway — when long context fraction rises, dense can win for p95 despite higher steady cost. that's why fallback exists.

mike: any telemetry we should add to make decisions safer in prod?

cheng: add these fields per-route and global:
- seqlen_histogram (buckets: 1,16,64,128,256,512,1024+)
- kv_page_fault_rate (1m,5m)
- in_flight_prefetch_count
- kernel_switch_count (rate)

sara: what about autotune offline vs online?

cheng: hybrid. offline sweep seeds initial thresholds per arch/model combo. online tuner adjusts thresholds slowly with the hysteresis rules above. also keep a lightweight shadow run for candidate kernels on 1% traffic to validate.

yousef: any quick TODOs?

cheng: yeah:
1) infra: add in_flight_prefetch_count metric + kv_page_fault_rate (infra@)
2) bench: run A/B shadow for kvstripe+128 on A100 prod-like traces (bench team)
3) runtime: implement hysteresis logic + cool-down + manual override
4) product: doc defaults and per-customer opt-out

mike: +1 to all. can you file quick tickets? :thumbsup:

cheng: will do. filing PRD + tickets today. attaching raw perf csv to the ticket (not in slack). thanks everyone.
